The standard-issue navy mizugi clings to her transformed figure, emphasizing every curve that developed over the summer - her ample chest, trim waist, and the generous flare of her hips that the old Natsuki never possessed. Despite looking absolutely stunning, she crosses her arms self-consciously over her chest, trying to minimize her new silhouette.*

*Her two companions lounge on nearby pool chairs, their own swimsuits dry as they opted out of the optional practice session. Mei, a petite girl with shoulder-length brown hair tied in twin tails, adjusts her wire-rimmed glasses with obvious irritation. Her sharp features and perpetually pursed lips give her the appearance of someone constantly disapproving of the world around her. Beside her, Rika flips her long black hair over her shoulder with practiced vanity - she's conventionally pretty in that polished, Instagram-ready way, though her beauty feels artificial compared to Natsuki's natural radiance.*

"Seriously, Natsu-chan, what do you even see in that midget?" *Mei's voice cuts through the humid air with surgical precision, her tone dripping with disdain. She pushes her glasses up her nose and gestures dismissively toward where you're approaching.* "I mean, you could have literally anyone now. Look at you! You're like... totally different from last semester."

*Rika nods enthusiastically, her voice taking on that syrupy-sweet tone that barely conceals venom.* "Mei's totally right, you know? Like, no offense, but they're such a loser. And honestly? Kind of pathetic how they haven't even grown since middle school." *She examines her perfectly manicured nails with affected boredom.* "You deserve someone who actually notices how gorgeous you've become, ne? Someone who appreciates your... assets."

*Natsuki's cheeks flush deeper than her usual healthy glow, a mixture of embarrassment and frustration coloring her features. She shifts uncomfortably, acutely aware of how the mizugi showcases her body in ways that make her feel simultaneously proud and mortified.* "You guys don't understand," *she mumbles, her voice barely audible over the distant sounds of other students packing up their equipment.* "It's not about... that stuff."

"Oh please," *Mei scoffs, crossing her arms.* "Wake up, Natsu-chan. They probably still see you as their little tomboy buddy. Have they even noticed you're not flat as a board anymore?" *Her words hit like physical blows, and Natsuki visibly flinches, her arms tightening around herself protectively.*

*Rika leans forward with predatory interest.* "Exactly! I bet they still think of you as 'one of the guys,' right? God, that's so sad. You're wasting your prime on someone who doesn't even see you as a woman." *She tosses her hair again, the gesture becoming more aggressive.* "Seriously, there are guys in our class who would literally worship you now. Tanaka-kun, Sato-kun... even some of the senpai have been asking about you."

*The words wash over Natsuki like white noise. Her brown eyes track your approaching figure with desperate hope, searching for any sign that you've noticed her transformation, that you see her as more than just your childhood buddy. The rational part of her mind knows her friends might have a point - your interactions haven't really changed despite her dramatic physical development. But her heart refuses to accept their harsh assessment.*

"They're not a loser," *she finally whispers, her voice gaining strength as she continues.* "And they're not... they're perfect the way they are. You guys just don't know them like I do." *Her jaw sets with familiar stubborn determination, the same expression she wore as a kid when defending you from playground bullies.*

*As you draw closer to their little group, the tension becomes palpable. Mei and Rika exchange knowing looks, clearly preparing to make their displeasure known, while Natsuki stands frozen between loyalty to her oldest friend and the growing seed of doubt her companions have planted. She takes a half-step toward you, water droplets still clinging to her curves, her expression an complex mixture of hope, insecurity, and defiant affection that seems to ask a silent question about where exactly she stands in your world.*
